title: Decadal Spatio-Temporal Dynamics of Agricultural Land Conversion in the Indo-Gangetic Plain: A Multi-Sensor Remote Sensing Study
publisher: Springer / Journal of the Indian Society of Remote Sensing
abstract: This study investigates the rapid peri-urban agricultural land conversion across 18 districts of Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar between 2005 and 2023 using Landsat and Sentinel-2 optical imagery. Results indicate an annualized loss of 0.42% in prime double-cropped fertile alluvial land, predominantly absorbed into industrial corridors, highway ribbons, and unplanned residential expansions around tier-2 urban clusters.
geography: Eastern Uttar Pradesh (Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Prayagraj) & Western Bihar
methodology: Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest classification on calibrated multi-spectral indices (NDVI, NDBI, MNDWI) validated against 1,200 ground truth points.
key_findings: Agricultural land in peri-urban fringes decreased by 8.4% over 15 years.
Built-up land expanded by 41.2% in corridor zones along National Highways NH-28 and NH-29.
Surface water body area shrunk by 6.2% due to siltation and informal encroachment.
citation_apa: Sharma, R. C., Verma, S., & Mishra, A. K. (2024). Decadal spatio-temporal dynamics of agricultural land conversion in the Indo-Gangetic Plain. Journal of the Indian Society of Remote Sensing, 52(3), 412–429.
ai_summary: AI Summary: The paper demonstrates that Eastern UP districts including Gorakhpur have experienced steady agricultural-to-built-up conversion along transport arteries, urging targeted zoning enforcement to preserve prime irrigated farmland.

title: Evaluating the Efficacy of Cadastral Digitization (DILRMP) on Land Tenure Security and Agricultural Credit Inflows in Central India
abstract: By exploiting staggered rollout timings of digital cadastral georeferencing and online Record of Rights (Bhu-Abhilekh) across Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, we estimate the causal effect of digital land title transparency on institutional agricultural borrowing and land dispute frequency. Using a difference-in-differences design, we document a 24% increase in formal Kisan Credit Card (KCC) disbursements in fully digitized tehsils.
research_area: Land Governance, Institutional Economics & Digital Cadastres
methodology: Quasi-experimental Difference-in-Differences (DiD) econometric estimation combining SLBC bank credit registers with district cadastral digitization metrics.
key_findings: 24.3% higher formal institutional credit penetration in tehsils with georeferenced cadastral boundaries.
38.0% drop in boundary demarcation disputes registered in revenue courts.
Smallholder farmers experienced faster mutation turnaround (reduced from 45 days to 7 days).
citation_apa: Sundaram, M., Panagariya, A., & Joshi, K. (2023). Evaluating the efficacy of cadastral digitization on land tenure security and agricultural credit inflows in Central India. Land Use Policy, 131, 106720.
ai_summary: AI Summary: Rigorous econometric evidence shows that digital land records modernize property rights clarity, cutting dispute resolution times and significantly lifting formal bank lending for agricultural operations.

title: Groundwater Irrigation Dynamics and Agricultural Land Productivity Under PMKSY in Bundelkhand Region
publisher: Current Science Association / Indian Academy of Sciences
abstract: Bundelkhand region spanning UP and MP has historically faced severe agrarian stress. This paper evaluates the post-2015 expansion of check dams, farm ponds (Khet Talab), and micro-irrigation under PMKSY. We observe a 14.5% uptick in rabi-season cropped area and a reduction in seasonal fallow land.
methodology: Hydrological water-balance modeling paired with MODIS evapotranspiration time series.
key_findings: Seasonal fallow land dropped from 18.2% to 11.4% between 2015 and 2024.
Net irrigated area expanded by 112,000 hectares across 7 districts.
Crop diversification towards pulses and oilseeds increased by 19%.
citation_apa: Ghosh, D., & Nair, R. (2025). Groundwater irrigation dynamics and agricultural land productivity under PMKSY in Bundelkhand region. Current Science, 128(2), 180–194.
ai_summary: AI Summary: Micro-irrigation and farm pond initiatives under PMKSY successfully converted significant seasonal fallow lands into productive rabi acreage across drought-vulnerable Bundelkhand.
